item.summary: perf(plugins): enforce load-once — default credential-source gate and containment registry reuse (#128639) Audit of the plugin load-once invariant found two owner defects. First, the credential-source gate from #69479 (skip plugin usage-auth without a config/env/profile-store credential source) became dead code when #78456 removed its last caller, so every usage read imported every usage-capable provider plugin's runtime on the request path — live-measured at 9 registry loads and 20.7s for one usage.status RPC on a fresh gateway. The flag is deleted and the gate is now the only behavior; the caller-prepared auth store is threaded through instead of being re-read from disk. Second, getLoadedRuntimePluginRegistry only reused the active registry on an exact load-option cache-key match, which no scoped runtime caller can satisfy against the gateway's composition-root key. It now falls through to the runtime-containment check when the caller names explicit plugin ids; unscoped requests keep exact-key semantics. Live proof (isolated dist gateway, 25-RPC sweep): post-startup registry loads 10 -> 2 (memory-plugin lazy-once only); usage.status 20,726ms -> 55ms. Regression tests fail pre-fix
